name: shader-pulsing-border
title: Pulsing Border
description: A glowing, pulsing frame of light runs around the edges of the frame and leaves the center clear for content, drawn in WebGL.
useWhen: You want a pulsing lit frame around the scene edges to contain foreground content.
A premium reveal benefits from an edge glow that leaves the center clear for text.
You want corner radius and thickness tunable via `roundness` and `thickness`.
avoidWhen: The brief bans decorative glow: keep `bloom` and `intensity` restrained so the border does not read as neon.
You want a full-field texture: the interior stays mostly the background color; use a noise or gradient shader.
The scene already has a strong border or frame in the layout.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Speed
variables.description: How fast it moves. 0 holds still.

variables.label: Colors
variables.description: Up to 5 colors, comma separated, that travel around the border.

variables.label: Background
variables.description: Color inside and outside the border.

variables.label: Thickness
variables.description: How thick the lit border is.

variables.label: Softness
variables.description: How soft the border edge is.

variables.label: Spots
variables.description: Number of light spots traveling around the border.

variables.label: Smoke
variables.description: Smoke that drifts inside the border.

variables.label: Smoke size
variables.description: How large the smoke shapes are.

variables.label: Margin
variables.description: Space between the frame edge and the border.

variables.label: Scale
variables.description: Zooms the shader in or out.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Lower renders faster; raise it when fine detail looks soft.
